Rochdale's population increased by around 12,100 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population passed 220,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Rochdale increased by 5.7%, from around 211,700 in 2011 to around 223,800 in 2021.

The population here increased by a greater percentage than the overall population of the North West (5.2%), but by a smaller percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, Rochdale was home to around 10.1 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 9.6 in 2011. This area was among the top 40% most densely populated English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was higher in Rochdale than across the North West

Median age stable in Rochdale

The latest census data also show that the average (median) age remained 38 years in Rochdale between the last two censuses.

This area had a lower average (median) age than the North West as a whole in 2021 (40 years) and a lower average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 65 to 74 years rose by around 4,500 (an increase of 27.3%), while the number of residents between 20 and 24 years fell by around 1,800 (12.9% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 65 and 74 years increased by 1.6 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Rochdale residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 185,900 Rochdale residents said they were born in England. This represented 83.1% of the local population. The figure has risen from around 184,400 in 2011, which at the time represented 87.1% of Rochdale's population.

Pakistan was the next most represented, with around 12,300 Rochdale residents reporting this country of birth (5.5%). This figure was up from just over 9,100 in 2011, which at the time represented 4.3% of the population of Rochdale.

The number of Rochdale residents born in Poland rose from around 2,000 in 2011 (1.0% of the local population) to just over 3,000 in 2021 (1.3%).

In 2021, 83.1% of Rochdale residents reported their country of birth as England

More lone parents

Rochdale saw the North West's largest percentage-point rise in the proportion of lone-parent households (from 13.0% in 2011 to 14.5% in 2021).

Oldham saw the North West's next largest increase in the percentage of lone-parent households (from 13.1% in 2011 to 14.4% in 2021).

The percentage of households including a lone parent in Rochdale increased by 1.4 percentage points

Fall in social renting

Rochdale saw the North West's second-largest percentage-point fall in the proportion of households in the social rented sector (from 23.1% in 2011 to 20.9% in 2021).

Across the region, only Salford saw a greater fall in the percentage of households in the social rented sector (from 28.8% to 25.4%).

Despite the decrease, Rochdale was in the highest 20% of English local authority areas for the share of households in the social rented sector in 2021.

The rate of social renting in Rochdale decreased by 2.3 percentage points

Disability in Rochdale

Rochdale saw the North West's joint third-largest percentage-point fall (alongside Bolton and Manchester) in the proportion of residents who were identified as disabled and limited a little (from 11.6% in 2011 to 10.7% in 2021). These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

Across the region, only Pendle (from 11.5% to 9.8%) and Blackburn with Darwen (from 11.6% to 10.3%) saw a greater decrease in the proportion of residents who were identified as disabled and limited a little.

Across the North West, the proportion of residents who were identified as disabled and limited a little remained 10.7%, while the proportion in nearby Rossendale increased from 10.6% to 11.0%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a little in Rochdale decreased by 0.9 percentage points

National identity in Rochdale

The increase in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK was greater in Rochdale (3.3 percentage points) than in nearby Rossendale (0.4 percentage points).

In Rochdale, the percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity increased from 5.1% in 2011 to 8.4% in 2021. During the same period, the percentage in nearby Rossendale increased from 1.9% to 2.3%.

The percentage of people who identified with a UK and non-UK national identity in Rochdale increased from 0.7% to 1.3%, while the percentage of people who identified as "British only" increased from 19.8% to 60.7%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in Rochdale increased by 3.3 percentage points

Fall in unemployment

In 2021, 3.3% of Rochdale residents (aged 16 years and over) said they were unemployed. This figure decreased from 5.4% in 2011.

In 2021, just over one in two people (52.6%) said they were employed (excluding full-time students), compared with 52.9% in 2011. The percentage of retired Rochdale residents decreased from 20.4% to 20.1%.

The decrease in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were unemployed was greater in Rochdale (2.2 percentage points) than across the North West (1.5 percentage points, from 4.2% to 2.8%). Across England, the percentage fell by 1.1 percentage points, from 4.0% to 2.9%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were unemployed (excluding full-time students) in Rochdale decreased by 2.2 percentage points

More adults worked short hours

In 2021, 8.5% of Rochdale residents aged 16 years and over and in employment said they worked 15 hours or less per week. This figure increased from 7.4% in 2011.

In 2021, around 1 in 12 people (8.3%) said they worked over 49 hours per week, compared with 9.7% in 2011. The percentage of adults in employment working 31 to 48 hours per week increased from 61.6% to 62.5%.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week was greater in Rochdale (1.1 percentage points) than across the North West (0.5 percentage points, from 9.1% to 9.6%). Across England, the percentage increased by 0.6 percentage points, from 9.7% to 10.3%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults who worked 15 hours or less in Rochdale increased by 1.1 percentage points

Unpaid care in Rochdale

In 2021, 4.1% of Rochdale residents (aged five years and over) reported providing up to 19 hours of unpaid care each week. This figure decreased from 7.1% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The decrease in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Rochdale (3.0 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the North West (2.7 percentage points, from 7.2% to 4.5%). Across England, the proportion fell by 2.8 percentage points, from 7.2% to 4.4%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Rochdale decreased by 3.0 percentage points

Ethnic groups in Rochdale

In 2021, 18.5% of Rochdale residents identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category, up from 14.9% in 2011. The 3.6 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across the North West, the percentage of people from the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" ethnic group increased from 6.2% to 8.4%, while across England the percentage increased from 7.8% to 9.6%.

In 2021, 74.0% of people in Rochdale identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 81.7% in 2011), while 3.5% identified their ethnic group within the "Black, Black British, Black Welsh, Caribbean or African" category (compared with 1.3% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category increased from 1.7% in 2011 to 2.4% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.

In 2021, 18.5% of usual residents in Rochdale identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category

Religion in Rochdale

In 2021, 28.8% of Rochdale residents reported having "No religion", up from 18.9% in 2011. The rise of 9.9 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in Rochdale. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across the North West, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 19.8% to 32.6%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 46.9% of people in Rochdale described themselves as Christian (down from 60.6%), while 18.8% described themselves as Muslim (up from 13.9% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

Read the bulletin Religion, England and Wales: Census 2021.

In 2021, 28.8% of usual residents in Rochdale reported having "No religion"

Health in Rochdale

In 2021, 44.1% of Rochdale residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 40.9% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" rose from 33.7% to 33.8%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Rochdale residents describing their health as "very bad" decreased from 1.9% to 1.5%, while those describing their health as "bad" fell from 6.7% to 5.5%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

The percentage of people in very bad health in Rochdale decreased by 0.4 percentage points

More adults never married or in a civil partnership

Of Rochdale residents aged 16 years and over, 38.5% said they had never been married or in a civil partnership in 2021, up from 35.1% in 2011.

In 2021, just over 4 in 10 people (43.2%) said they were married or in a registered civil partnership, compared with 44.4% in 2011. The percentage of adults in Rochdale that had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership decreased from 9.7% to 9.3%.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership was greater across the North West (3.8 percentage points, from 35.6% to 39.4%) than in Rochdale (3.4 percentage points). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.3 percentage points, from 34.6% to 37.9%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who had never married or registered a civil partnership in Rochdale increased by 3.4 percentage points
